sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Introduces the Bangkok workshop on CD4 T lymphocyte counting, citing the HIV burden in the South-East Asia Region and the need for CD4 testing to guide antiretroviral therapy. It notes that sixteen laboratory professionals from seven countries attended, facilitated by Siriraj Hospital and India's National AIDS Research Institute.

sections.extract: Introduction The AIDS epidemic continues to spread across the South-East Asia (SEA) Region, which is the most affected part of the world after sub-Saharan Africa. To date, around 40 million people around the world have been infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), the virus that causes AIDS. Of them more than six million are in the SEA Region. sections.title: Objectives

summary.text: Lists the workshop's four objectives, from reviewing CD4 enumeration status to hands-on training and planning external quality assessment.

sections.extract: Objectives The objectives of the workshop were to: (1) Review the status of enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes in high HIV-burden Member countries of the SEA Region; (2) Orient on new, economical and field-friendly technologies for CD4 enumeration; (3) Provide hands-on training on selected technologies including the interpretation of results, and (4) Identify a mechanism for external quality assessment scheme.

sections.title: Inaugural session

summary.text: Summarizes the opening of the CD4 workshop, where speakers stressed the importance of CD4 counts for antiretroviral treatment and of quality assurance. Participants were encouraged to learn about the various technologies so they could choose one suited to their infrastructure and resources.

sections.extract: Inaugural session The Dean of the medical faculty at Siriraj Hospital welcomed the participants. In his inaugural remarks, he emphasized that CD4 enumeration technology is critical for effective implementation of any programme on antiretroviral therapy as well as for providing efficient care to the patient. sections.title: Country reports

summary.text: Outlines the workshop's working methods and then reports on the status of CD4 T lymphocyte enumeration in participating countries such as Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. The country reports cover available equipment, laboratories performing counts, training and participation in quality assessment schemes. Thailand's report notes training courses run by Siriraj Hospital's centre of excellence and a national institute since 2004.

sections.title: Presentations and topics for discussions

summary.text: Summarizes the technical presentations at the workshop, beginning with the role of CD4 counts in HIV pathogenesis, disease monitoring and decisions on starting antiretroviral therapy. Further talks explain flow cytometry principles, gating strategies such as panleucogating, low-cost and alternative counting methods, and haematology analysers. It concludes that the choice of method should depend on test volume, staff, support and cost, with validation and proficiency testing before routine use.

sections.title: Group work

summary.text: Describes a generic plan drafted by participants for a national external quality assessment scheme for CD4 counting, covering responsibilities, infrastructure, training and specimen logistics.

sections.extract: Group work Participants developed a generic plan for the establishment of a national external quality assessment scheme for CD4 T lymphocytes enumeration. sections.title: Hands-on enumeration of CD4 T Lymphocytes

summary.text: Notes that participants were shown and performed flow cytometric CD4 counting and that a final open session reviewed topics and country-specific issues.

sections.extract: Hands-on enumeration of CD4 T Lymphocytes All participants were demonstrated flow cytometry techniques using FACSCount and Tritest on FACSCalibur. The tests were also performed by the Report of a Workshop Page 12 participants themselves. The facilitators discussed various issues, commonly encountered problems and ways to obviate these. sections.title: For WHO

summary.text: Lists recommendations for WHO, including guidelines and procedures for CD4 enumeration, expansion of the regional quality scheme and criteria for paediatric use.

sections.extract: For WHO The following actions were recommended for WHO: (1) WHO should develop guidelines and standard operating procedure for CD4 T lymphocytes enumeration. (2) WHO should support the expansion of Regional CD4 T lymphocytes EQAS to Sri Lanka, Myanmar, and Nepal in addition to India, Indonesia and Thailand where it is already in operation. sections.title: For Member States

summary.text: Lists recommendations for Member countries on CD4 testing infrastructure, joining the regional quality scheme, establishing local baseline values and equipment maintenance.

sections.extract: For Member States The following were recommended for Member countries: (1) Member countries should accord priority to establish infrastructure for CD4 T lymphocytes enumeration to provide effective support to ART programmes. summary.text: Describes the closing session, where participants valued the meeting and WHO staff thanked the Thai hosts and facilitators.

sections.extract: Concluding session WHO’s initiative in organizing this meeting was appreciated in the concluding session.
